issues.legal_issue: A person invoking public interest jurisdiction must act bona fide and not as a proxy for private or other oblique interests.
material_facts: The applicant brought a challenge to a land lease in the name of public interest, but the Court found material connecting him and the person representing him with a competitor of the lessee.

The applicant’s disclosed financial resources did not explain the substantial litigation expenses, and the claimed donations and the role of an associated society raised questions about the funding of the litigation.
The Court found that the applicant had been set up by others and was a name lender, but nevertheless examined the evidence concerning the land’s status.
issues.conclusion: The application was mala fide and was dismissed with costs for abuse of the process of law.
issues.legal_principle: Public interest standing is available to bona fide litigants, not to persons acting for personal gain, private profit, political motivation, or other oblique considerations. Courts must guard against misuse of public interest litigation by proxies and busybodies. The Court relied on S.P. Gupta v. Union of India, Janata Dal v. H.S. Chowdhary, Dattaraj Nathuji Thaware v. State of Maharashtra, State of Maharashtra v. Prabhu, Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation v. GAR Re-Rolling Mills, and Dr. B.K. Subbarao v. K. Parasaran.

predicates.public_interest_litigation: A person brings a proceeding asking the court to act in the public interest.
predicates.applicant_is_proxy_for_private_interest: The applicant acts on behalf of another person or interest rather than pursuing the stated public cause independently.
predicates.litigation_funding_is_inconsistent_with_: The costs of pursuing the proceeding substantially exceed the applicant’s disclosed financial means, and the source of support does not credibly explain that gap.
predicates.applicant_has_links_to_private_beneficia: The applicant or the person acting for the applicant has links to a private party that would benefit from the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a person brings a public interest proceeding as a proxy for a private interest and the funding or connections support that finding, the proceeding may be rejected as mala fide with costs.

issues.legal_issue: An empowered committee assisting the court in forest matters may examine and report facts relevant to the bona fides of a public interest applicant.
material_facts: The Central Empowered Committee had been appointed to assist the Court on matters concerning depletion, preservation, and conservation of forests.
The Committee’s reports discussed facts relevant to the applicant’s bona fides, including his representation and connections to a business competitor of the lessee.
The applicant contended that the Committee had exceeded its authority by addressing his bona fides.
issues.conclusion: The Committee did not exceed its authority; given its assigned responsibilities, it had a duty to point out facts relevant to an applicant’s bona fides.
issues.legal_principle: A committee appointed to assist the Court on forest conservation issues may, and in carrying out its assigned responsibilities must, identify facts relevant to determining the bona fides of a person invoking public interest jurisdiction. The Court applied the public interest litigation principles discussed in S.P. Gupta v. Union of India, Janata Dal v. H.S. Chowdhary, and Dattaraj Nathuji Thaware v. State of Maharashtra.

predicates.forest_conservation_assistance_proceedin: The proceeding concerns forest conservation and is being considered with assistance from a committee appointed by the court.
predicates.committee_is_assigned_to_assist_the_cour: The court has assigned a committee responsibility to assist it on issues arising in the proceeding.
predicates.applicant_bona_fides_are_relevant_to_the: Facts about whether an applicant is acting bona fide bear on the court’s consideration of the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a court-appointed committee assists in a forest conservation proceeding and the applicant’s bona fides are relevant, the committee must report relevant facts about those bona fides.

issues.legal_issue: Whether land is forest land for the purposes of the forest conservation regime depends on its character and government records, not merely its ownership or classification, assessed against the evidence of the particular parcel.
material_facts: The dispute concerned land leased for a coal washery, and the parties disputed whether the parcel was forest land.

Historical settlement records and maps did not establish that the area had merged with the adjoining village; the maps placed the parcel in a separate area, and the Court found no reason to depart from the Central Empowered Committee’s assessment of those records.

The Central Empowered Committee’s later reports relied on satellite imagery and expert examination; the Court accepted the resulting evidence that the parcel did not meet the applicable description of a deemed forest.
The Court found no substance in the claim that the parcel was forest land and accepted the Committee’s second and third reports.
issues.conclusion: The land was not forest land, and the Central Empowered Committee’s recommendations on that point were accepted.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(i) of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, as interpreted in T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India, ‘forest’ is understood according to its dictionary meaning and includes statutorily recognised forests and areas recorded as forest in government records, irrespective of ownership. In that case the Court considered Ambica Quarry Works v. State of Gujarat and Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra v. State of U.P. The Court assessed the historical records and expert evidence in this case, including the remote-sensing material, and held that the parcel did not qualify as a deemed forest.

predicates.forest_status_determination: A court is determining whether a parcel is forest land.
predicates.historical_records_do_not_place_parcel_w: The available historical records do not identify the parcel as part of a recorded forest.
predicates.maps_place_parcel_outside_adjacent_villa: The relevant maps place the parcel outside the adjacent village area claimed to include it as forest.
predicates.expert_satellite_evidence_shows_parcel_b: Expert satellite analysis indicates that the parcel does not satisfy the characteristics used to identify the relevant category of deemed forest.

issues.definition: When a court is determining forest status and the historical records, maps, and expert satellite evidence do not establish that the parcel has the relevant forest characteristics, the parcel is not forest land.
